inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' add-back; EquityAwardTaxes confirmed nil (verified in kpis table, no net-share-settlement cash tax withholding disclosed)
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2025 and H1-2026 buybacks were $0 (FY2023 saw a large $149.1m buyback that has since lapsed); historically buybacks (FY2020-2023, cumulative ~$175m) plus modest issuance kept the share count flat 700-745m for a decade, so flat-share-count is used as the base assumption rather than mechanically applying max(0, sbc-buyback) each year, which would imply a small dilution the company has not historically allowed to persist
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt is net cash of $896.9m (H1-2026 cash, zero debt) LESS the pending $300m special dividend (announced, subject to SAMR approval + MVM divestment completion, both substantially achieved by early FY26 per company commentary but not yet paid as of H1-2026) = $596.9m net cash used in the EV bridge. This avoids overstating equity value with cash that is already economically committed to shareholders via a declared-but-unpaid special dividend.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FY2020 (peak, pre-daigou-collapse) and FY2021-2022 (daigou/China-channel collapse trough, ~$200m inventory write-downs) are structural outliers excluded from all CAGR baselines per company guidance. 5-year revenue CAGR (1.9%, FY2020-2025) is distorted by starting at the pre-collapse peak; 3-year CAGR (9.3%, FY2023-2025) is the cleaner post-recovery trend and is used as the historical anchor, though the FY26 explicit forecast is guidance-driven (mid-double-digit %) rather than a mechanical CAGR extrapolation. Reported FCF 3yr CAGR (39.9%) is far above owner FCF 3yr CAGR (55.8% off a very depressed FY2023 base distorted by a $26.7m interest income spike and inventory rebuild) - neither is a reliable growth-rate input; revenue and EBITDA-margin components drive the projection instead. Equity CAGR is distorted by the FY25 dividend policy inception and pending special dividend and is not used as the growth driver.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is small for ATM.NZ (~0.6-1.6% of revenue historically, well below the FCF base) so SBC-driven dilution is not a material growth-rate distortion here, unlike SBC-heavy tech names. The dominant adjustment for ATM.NZ is the interest income strip: FY2025 interest income of $45.5m equals 23% of reported FCF ($197.5m) and would double-count the $896.9m cash pile if left inside FCF while cash is also added to EV.

memo.note: SBC is immaterial for ATM.NZ (~0.7% of revenue) so the base-vs-non-cash-SBC IV spread is small (~$0.17/share) - the SBC treatment choice is NOT what drives this valuation. The dominant driver of the gap between intrinsic value and the $8.25 market price is (a) stripping ~$40-45m/yr of interest income that the market appears to still be capitalizing inside reported FCF/earnings multiples, (b) the multi-year Pokeno insourcing capex program ($50-70m/yr guided, elevated vs historical $3-20m capex) depressing near-term owner FCF conversion, and (c) the market currently pricing ATM.NZ at ~19.7x FY2025 EV/EBITDA and ~37-39x owner FCF, well above the DCF's implied base-case exit multiple of 12.4x EBITDA-equivalent FCF - i.e. the market is assuming a materially higher sustained multiple than this DCF grants a mature, China-birth-rate-exposed consumer staple.

warnings: Market price ($8.25) implies a valuation the base-case DCF cannot reach even in the bull scenario ($6.22) - this reflects the DCF's structural discount for (1) interest-income double-count removal, (2) heavy multi-year Pokeno capex, and (3) a terminal growth rate capped at 2.25% reflecting the structurally shrinking China IMF category (declining birth rates). Readers should treat the gap as the model's explicit view that ATM.NZ trades on growth/multiple-expansion assumptions this DCF does not grant, not as a data error.

H1-2026 reported net income ($8.4m) is heavily distorted by a $103.7m after-tax loss on discontinued operations (MVM divestment); continuing-operations profit for H1-2026 was $112.1m (H1-2025 continuing-ops pcp restated at $102.5m per the FY2026 interim accounts), which is the figure used for trend analysis, not the headline consolidated NPAT.

The pending $300m special dividend is treated as an economic distribution already committed to shareholders and is netted out of cash in the EV bridge (net_debt = -$596.9m, not -$896.9m). If the special dividend is delayed or reduced, intrinsic value per share would rise by up to ~$0.41/share (300/729).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (historical and implied); will not match published GAAP P/E from screeners. FY-end = June monthly close from Yahoo 10y series.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base IV $4.44 implies 17.0x SBC-adjusted P/E and 8.5x EV/EBITDA vs ex-outlier historical averages of 35.3x and 22.3x — the model concludes the market pays a premium the owner-FCF stream does not support (interest income on ~$900m net cash stripped, $300m pending special dividend netted out, China IMF demographic deceleration). IV below market is a documented model conclusion, not an over-valuation error; the trip conditions guard only against DCF over-valuation.
